# Mirror of the organisation's Actions allow-list (Settings > Actions > Policies).
#
# It is a COPY, and the workflow that reads it says so: the API that serves the
# real list needs an org-admin scope that GITHUB_TOKEN does not have, so CI
# cannot read the authority directly. Refresh it with:
#
#   gh api orgs/bymaxone/actions/permissions/selected-actions --jq '.patterns_allowed[]'
#
# Why it exists: a `uses:` outside the allow-list is rejected when a workflow
# STARTS, so the whole file is refused -- startup_failure, no jobs, no logs. This
# repository publishes reusable workflows and consumes none of them, so the first
# execution of anything it ships is in another repository, after a release. That
# is how one such reference took every node-lib-ci consumer's CI down.
#
# github-owned (actions/*) and same-org (bymaxone/*) references are allowed by
# policy without appearing here.
#
# Staleness is only safe in one direction. A pattern added to the policy but
# missing here fails a reference that would work -- loud and harmless. A pattern
# REMOVED from the policy but left here passes a reference consumers will reject
# at startup, and this file cannot detect that on its own. Refresh it whenever
# the organisation policy narrows.
pnpm/action-setup@*
actions-rust-lang/setup-rust-toolchain@*
Swatinem/rust-cache@*
taiki-e/install-action@*
ossf/scorecard-action@*
dtolnay/rust-toolchain@*
dorny/paths-filter@*
stefanzweifel/git-auto-commit-action@*
docker/build-push-action@*
docker/login-action@*
docker/metadata-action@*
docker/setup-buildx-action@*
trufflesecurity/trufflehog@*
appleboy/ssh-action@*

# --- owners covered by `verified_allowed: true` rather than by a pattern ---
#
# The policy also admits verified marketplace creators, and that set is not
# enumerable through any endpoint CI can reach. These are the ones this
# organisation actually references, each confirmed by a green run rather than by
# assumption -- OSV-Scanner completes successfully in nest-queue and nest-auth,
# and it uses two of them. Add an owner here only with the same evidence.
verified:github
verified:google
verified:step-security
